data: It's still a really fun game, I would definitely get it on sale
10/10 replayability and the story is just perfect (You make it on your own lol)
I really like the overall gameplay, its very fun, complex, challenging, and unique
Really fun game and it's easy to mod
My only complaint is that the DLCs are a bit pricey for the amount of content they add
It's just not worth the money
Do not buy this game, it is unplayable
I cannot recommend it to anyone until Paradox stops being a greedy developer and publisher
I do not recommend the base game, as it lacks almost all content that is locked behind a paywall
Ultimately a very disappointing game experience, because of the terrible game mechanics and RNG AI programming nonsense that ruins the gaming immersion and experience
Save yourself the money and time, and dont buy this slop

Do not encourage this kind of behavior from a publisher and do not purchase this game until Paradox stops this unhealthy pricing practice

Paradox has kinda got a bad reputation for over monetizing their games with dlcs, and this game is on that path. But, if you get it while it's still new, you will get to enjoy every new feature as a true upgrade to the game. That makes it feel a lot more worthwhile to buy the dlc. The only people who complain about the dlc costs are either spending someone else's money to buy it and got cut off, or don't buy the games when they are new and get the full experience. Sure, buy a 6 year old game and all the dlc that has come out over that span and you end up spending like 200 bucks. Or buy it now, pay 50, then buy the 20 buck dlcs as they came out instead of buying a new game that month. It doesn't sting that bad then guys, come on. And honestly, this is probably my favorite paradox game so far, and I fucking love Stellaris lol.

Easily the easiest paradox game out there. It is so fun to become stupidly overpowered and change history however you see fit. Obviously, wait until the game and it's DLC's are on sale, because paradox are greedy corporate scum.

Endless fun, what feels like an infinite ways to play. I recommend play all over the map. The game runs well, only crashes with mods. Also the mod community is amazing. Almost any improvement you think of someone else has. So many full conversion mods I mean it when i say this is the only game ive played for years and i play all the time.

Spend 3 hours playing the tutorial on pause, reading tool tips inside tool tips just to open new tool tips to understand other tool tips, all thanks to tool tips. After 3 hours of tool tipping I was thrown into the cold water next to the island of Ireland. Spend 7 hours to conquer and unite the island. At the age of 63, 10 hours into the game and somewhere around 3 am in the morning, looking over my kingdom and my happy vassals, I died a peaceful death, bequeath my title to my oldest son, only to see him f*** up everything after 30 minutes of gameplay. 11/10 here I go again. Playing my other son, trying to reunite the kingdom again. This time for an endless glory! Hail Mc tool tips!
Just a true Joy to play. Create your story, create your dynasty, create your fun. This game truly goes as deep as you want it and only in as much of quantity as you'd like.

Easiest grand strategy to get into IMO. I enjoy the role play elements of the game and the various actions able to be taken through the mighty ruler you'll become... unless you're a peasant with only 1 county of course that wants to be a vassal of a mighty kingdom!

Pull the trigger already!
Best paradox game imo u can do a lot of stuff which is good just before playing this get a good pc
The best medieval experience game currently. Fluid and fun gameplay, I highly recommend it, especially for beginners of strategy games of this style.

One of the top 5 strategy games I've played in my life. I try to play other games but I always come back to this game. Great replay value if you think of each play through as crafting your own story. Characters and map feel alive. If you play this game like the sims, you will have a great time. Only criticism I have is late game content. There needs to be more interesting things to do once you get really powerful.

I really like how many different ways you can play this game, from map painter to roleplayer to bene gesserit succession planner to actual god-king. There's simply so many systems there's always some weird interaction to discover.

I wish I could recommend this game. The actual gameplay is awesome. The problem is that Paradox management seems to have let their QA go to complete trash over the last couple years, pretty much since the Royal Court release cycle. The Tournaments DLC released with bugs that completely broke the features that were the whole selling point, and they weren't fixed to the point that it was fully playable until literally the next DLC released. Then Wards DLC released and numerous users (including myself) reported the game crashing to desktop on loading a save game or ruler dying. Nearly two months later and Paradox hasn't even acknowledged the crashes as a known issue, let alone released a hotfix.

Customers have a right to expect that when they pay over a hundred dollars for a game + multiple DLC that the software will actually run as advertised.

I'm very much a fan of this games structure and foundation. After playing more than a hundred or so hours the game might start to become a little hollow without fun scenarios. Over time the game will receive more updates and dlc to flesh out the world. If you like Ck2 this game is for you.

One of the greatest games I have ever played. Every time I start a new game the hours simply fly by. You can easily spend 5 hours trying to take over a county, duchy, etc. and simply have it all lost after being assassinated or getting sick and dying early. Anything can happen, and will happen. This game is simply unique and truly fascinating.

I am definitely more of a casual gamer and have still put nearly 200 hours into this. i like a lot of management games, Football Manager, Pro Cycling Manager, dynasty modes of NBA etc so this really suited my style of game as I travel a lot. i became utterly obsessed. If you are a history buff or just really into strategy this is the game for you

fun game for singleplayer but the multiplayer is incredibly fucked.
you constantly get disconnected from either paradox or the games get out of sync and become unplayable.

Much less intimidating to start playing compared to Paradox's other grand strategy games. I used to play Medieval Total War and wish it could be less about battles and more about dynasties and diplomacy. This is basically my dream game

Crusaders Kings III is the first game of its genre I've tried out. 200 hrs in, I can say I'm hooked and I love it! 
The only real problem of this incredible game is the way the company behind it handles DLC content. It's very similar to the way Electronic Arts handles the Sims 4 imo. So be wary of that if that's something you care about.

In my opinion, this is one of the most realistic political strategy games ever made. The atmosphere is outstanding, the music fits perfectly, and the graphics are impressive for a game of this genre.

If you're looking for a strategy game that focuses more on political depth and decision-making rather than just constant battles and sword-fighting, this is the one. I'm not saying the war mechanics are bad—far from it—but the core of the game lies in governing, diplomacy, and managing your nation, rather than simply rushing to conquer everything like a careless child.

9/10
Game is AWESOME, but has a GROSS AND GREEDY DLC policy and the main game alone lacks A LOT (if it didn´t, you would not see a shitload of DLC).

The depth of this game, is deeper than the sea, its vastness is that of the infinite reaches of space. You can be a ruler, a tyrant, a philanderer, a legend, or a holy warrior. Or you can just marry your sister, marry off your kids to the highest bidder, or murder all the people who even look at your throne. Truly, a great game. There is a small drawback, this game is DEEP no joke and it can be VERY overwhelming but once you get the hang of the basics it is SO MUCH FUN. 10/10 from random middle aged gamer

although I've only played a bit (70h) I can say that this game is addicting and very complex game. I've come to a trend where I am enjoying more and more paradox games. great for individuals that love grand strategy like civ.

The team needs to take a break from new content and spend time being custodians of the game they've created. The old DLCs need to be polished and brought up to the current standard, they need to fix the near-constant desync'ing in multiplayer and take a hard look at the current state of the game before adding new content.

I have slightly over 100 hours in CK3 now, but I've never actually played CK3. I waited on buying CK3 until the Elder Kings 2 total conversion came out, and when it did, I bought it, and I have been playing nothing but EK2 since.

My thumbs up is more of a, CK3 is a cool base game that allows for great total conversion mods, rather than it's a good game on its own. I wouldn't know, never played it un-modded, probably never will.

Not as good as CKII, a bit boring in some parts of the game when you have a good knowledge of the game many mecanisms, and not convinced by many DLCs. The French traduction is pretty poor, too. That said, on the whole, it is still a good game, that will hopefully get better in time.

This is the only game I can recommend playing on Ironman. I don't know what it is about it, but this game has a SINCERE reward to failing. I've had multiple generations of the Rurik dynasty fall prey to murdering each other out of spite, and each time it provides an intense, enjoyable challenge to resolve the inevitable succession crises.

Incredibly fun game - I cannot wait for Paradox to keep expanding it!

This game is an all-around improvement on EVERYTHING from the previous game (including the DLCs). It runs smoother, it is prettier, and it feels more realistic. I like that they've taken a more personal approach with the game, structuring it more around you as a ruler rather than you as a country. I feel like that has always been the distinguishing feature of CK. Those seeking just to blob and war the whole map away will miss the best part of this game which is roleplaying a character and building a dynasty.

While Paradox has been infamous for cutting content out of their games to make more DLC, that is not the impression I get here at all. The game is extremely entertaining at its core and DLC from here on I can only imagine will serve purely to enhance different aspects of it (the one exception to this I can think of would be a Republics DLC, as you cannot play republics in the base game).

So yes, CKIII is very much Sims mixed with EUIV, however it is also so much more than that. Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys grand strategy, Roleplay, managerial games, or any combination of the three.

With all the DLC that has been added to Crusader Kings III it has been a great experience and the game is an easy recommendation. The game is still fun to play without DLC but you'll be missing out on a lot of great content.

My advice for anyone who considers buying Crusader Kings III. Wait for a sale and buy the game in a bundle with the DLC.

The real magic of Crusader Kings III lies in how it blends grand strategy with deep roleplay. Where most strategy titles focus on map painting and raw conquest, CK3 thrives on the stories that emerge from its characters. Rulers aren’t just names and portraits on a screen — they have ambitions, flaws, and eccentricities that shape every aspect of your reign. A brilliant general may secure victories on the battlefield but alienate the nobility with poor diplomacy. A pious zealot might inspire loyalty among the faithful, but plunge their realm into endless holy wars. These dynamics turn every campaign into a personal saga, where politics, intrigue, and family drama collide. Instead of just managing empires, you’re guiding lives, and that human element makes every dynasty feel unique and alive.

No game has taught me more about feudalism, and thanks to this game I now know that feudalism is without a doubt the worst form of government ever invented.

But in seriousness this game is excellent. I usually play multiplayer with friends and we just have a blast supporting and backstabbing each other. Our most recent playthrough has me as emperor, which I prefer because I like overall strategy and empire management, and doling out land to my friends being my vassals, lording over their smaller fiefs, which is their preferred style

Crusader Kings 3 is a mixed genre game for RPG and strategy. There is more tutorial than in CK2 but its still only text boxes. To atleast be able to play smart you need to play probably multiple hundred hours, but if it clicks its just amazing!

This game was kinda fun, but a little clunky, now it's near unplayable.
I get plagues every few years that kills all of my dynasty members and locks me up in my capital, disabling my ability to do anything.

Then i have entrenched regent mechanic that's broken and drains my prestige into the negative because the bugged out AI, that's in the -1000 or more, keeps spamming the sway power button endlessly. Can't even counter it because it takes two years to be allowed to press the button to counter them, yet they'll counter it in a few months and drive you both into prestige debt.

How did they manage to mess up this badly?

Despite taking the counter measures to survive and stop plagues, I'm still getting them every few years? Everyone dies quicker than I can replace them. It isn't even on high plague frequency.

Can't they make a single DLC that doesn't break the base game?

Can't recommend this game until they actual fix it.

There's nothing like disinheriting your son because he decided incest was wincest and had his way with his mother, giving her lovers pox in the process. Then 200 years later that cadet branch he apparently created, allies with some foreign super power and absolutely steam roles you. 10/10 a masterpiece.

CK3 is a fun game although it can feel overwhelming at times, I'm sure this is just the learning gap that I have yet too fully overcome. For what you are buying it for it accomplishes without flaw. Would recommend.

I am on IOS a 2020 M1 MacBook AIR running macOS 26.1.
This game does not run and does not start for me. I waited a good 30 minutes with a black screen for some music to start, then 15 more for nothing else. I've played the game on PS5 and was excited to run it on this laptop, however it took 35% of my battery just booting up.

Not sure about y'all but that sounds like allot of work. So I have requested a refund. I would not recommend this game. Unless of course, you are running windows on a decent PC, and if that is the case, buy right away.

I honestly don't see the point of this title. It's a watered-down CK2. There are some changes and new features, but they pale compared to CK2, even without the latter's full swathe of DLC content. The new graphics are nice, but any features added to CK3 are easily replicated by CK2 mods and the graphics don't make up for the lack of content within CK3. I bought this title at full price like a big dumbdumb and regret it immensely. I'm sure that, in time, CK3 will have new features added through patches and DLC, but the title as it is now is, imo, a waste of money.

Hands down the best grand strategy game I've ever played. One of the best games I've ever played. One of my favorite things about this game is that my first time playing it I had no idea what I was doing and still managed to have fun. Over time I learned the various systems of the game and how to shape my realm in the way I wanted to and it then became even more fun. CK3 is really a relationship builder more than anything and you will constantly find yourself building out and experiencing these elaborate story lines. I have hundreds of hours in this game and I am still finding situations that I have never seen before. It's one of few games I constantly find myself putting down for months at a time and then coming back to.

I am brand new to this Grand Strategy type of game from these developers and WOW so much fun! Awesome thing is I now have several games I can go back and play! This along with the AoE RTS games, and I am set. If anyone has suggestions on the best Grand Strategy game from these guys, let me know.

Update after 29 hours: I began the tutorial playing as Petty King of Munster in Ireland. I slowly fought my way to the kingdom of Ireland, and has a couple of small counts in England, and slowly fought my way to king of Alba as well. Well, after about 85 years of in-game time, I accidentally died without having passed off those duchies to the correct person, so I lost it. I then quit lol. Just came here to say, I played 29 hours off the tutorial game and didn't even explore or talk to 99% of the map. I also didn't have to quit, I just lost about 10 hours of work, so I decided I would quit and restart as a kingdom of my choice when I am ready. for now, gonna try out Hearts of Iron IV. This game is amazing though and it's very expansive. I bet with some mods/DLCs this would be even better. I just didn't want to redo that entire 10 hours of working to gain back that kingdom.

At a certain point it becomes annoying and frustrating, since the game literally just spams you with events at multiple positions on the screen, decisions (most of them are "shut up, i dont care) and neverending war (because if you beat 2 wars, meanwhile 2 others had been declared). My personal favourite is giving names to your cousins 8th child her 4th daughter - because these are descisions of real importance.

While I like a certain level of "having something to do" and "beeing challenged" this is just overwhelming as **** and not fun at all. Giving the player some space for catching a breath, despite his skills, would have been to much to ask for. The game just comes with the lube, no matter if you ready or not and it just won't stop.

I am not gonna lie it was difficult at first. However if you run a couple games learn from your mistakes and what you didn't know an run it back. You get hella into it and start creating massive dynasties or huge empires or kick it at a party. In conclusion if you like strategy and deception in a medieval setting this game is hella dope.

One of my good friends put me on to this game. I have over 175 hours on El Cinco (Ps5) and got the steam version so I can play to GoT mod, pretty fun game ngl gang. The DLC be trippin on the prices doe, like faaaa

This games OK,but seriously,can we try to over complicate things and go just a tad overboard?Incorporating clunky terminology is one thing,adding interfaces all over the place and putting a pause button on time doesn't help.I have had the series,from CK 1.It was ok at best then it still is and now goes stumbling into ridiculous.Only reason I never gave it more time?Disliked it.....and I am being generous.

This is my favorite game of all time. Even after 1000+ hours of playing it I still find myself gushing like a little girl because of the story unfolding in front of my eyes. Yes this is a fascinating game of strategy, but on top of that it builds stories better than RPGs and that's amazing.

Loved playing the game - the game is fun. 

Most of the dlc is fun. 

The way in which the company tries and milk every last penny out of its customers is disgusting - also when they roll out an inevitable new update. they will be gamebreaking for saves you've been working on for 300 hours. 

Thanks for sucking balls Paradox
The game is awesome , graphics are top notch , sound just pure joy , story line man you can choose whatever you wanna do and with the amount of mods available pure gem , id say its worth the money

Allowing gay marriage, clerical marriage, accepting witchcraft and banning divorce? Pope doesn't seem to mind at all.

Pragmatism much?

Apparently were all zealots who start drinking and lashing ourselves the moment our liege brings up conversion.

The only person who could find this DLC enjoyable is someone who (unironically) indulges in masochism.

First day playing: I'm struggling to understand how to play it. I might revise this after I learn how to play it, better. Right now I'm just blindly clicking the map, wondering how to move things forward. I play RTS a little, but this game isn't really your average RTS. I never played the prequels, pretty used to FPS and fighting games where the enjoyment is immediate and you don't have to watch a youtube tutorial on how to get started.

1/26 - There is a decent game here, it's a grand strategy game, I've never played one of those till now. I'm pretty confused by the amount of DLC, it feels like they left out features that should have been in the main game. Play the long tutorial, don't deviate from its instruction and read what it shows you closely.

1/28 - I feel like I can recommend the base game now. You have to have patience to learn it. Play the long tutorial and build from there. I do not recommend jumping into a game with a friend until you've conquered Ireland and get an rough idea of what this game is like.

Basically a Game of Thrones simulator. You’ve got everything from intrigues and backstabbing to love affairs and political scheming. You’ll spend hours building your dynasty, only to end up betrayed and killed by the ones you trusted the most. So yes, basically real life 1:1. Also, get the Game of Thrones mod if you’re a fan of the series. You’ll absolutely love it.

Very Nice and Educational.

Surprisingly, it is less of a strategy game and more of a life/social simulation game.
It is different in this regard from other popular paradox games, such as Hearts of Iron or Stellaris.

Great game, the series is one of my all-time favs. Just get the game and get lost in your own medieval world. Also, given the game is at the start of its life cycle, now is probably the best time to get into the game and follow the DLCs and expansions in the coming years. Buying full-fledged paradox titles towards the end of the life-cycle can be expensive.

Overall 10/10. Will recommend!

I dont know how to express my love-hate relationship with PDX but CK3 despite being one of the more/most shallow map games (reddit writing, goober warfare, little to no flavor, etc.) it is the most easy to tune out to and destroy your dopamine receptors. Low lows and high highs. The game will throw random mass disasters to ruin the run or it will literally just let you autopilot.

I also think the team on this game might have some mixed up priorities, mess up sometimes, but they are also the only PDX team to do anything to actually try and improve their game.
